questions.question: A PM writes: "Investigate why activation dropped." What is missing before a method can be chosen?
options: The choice this investigation could change, and its alternatives
A hypothesis about the likely cause
A deadline and an owner
Segmentation of the activation decline
questions.explanation: "Investigate why" is a topic, not a decision. Without the choice and its live alternatives, any method will produce findings nobody can act on. The most tempting distractor is D: segmentation is genuinely good practice, but it is a method selected before the decision exists, so its output cannot move anything.

questions.question: Which of these is an observation, with no interpretation attached?
options: Onboarding is confusing new users
The new signup flow hurt activation
Activation fell 11% over six weeks
Users don't understand the value of AI suggestions
questions.explanation: Only C states what was measured. A, B, and D each attach a cause to the observation. Smuggling the mechanism into the observation is how the first plausible story wins before it has been tested.

questions.question: You have written a decision statement. What is the sharpest test that it is genuinely decision-linked?
options: It fits on one page and names an owner
You can name two plausible findings that would lead to different actions
It cites the metric and the time window
Your engineering lead agrees it is worth investigating
questions.explanation: If every plausible finding leads to the same action, the evidence cannot change anything and the work is decoration. The other options are hygiene — useful, but they do not test the link between evidence and choice.

questions.question: A PM is entering a genuinely new market and cannot name the decision the research will change. What does decision-first require?
options: Write a decision statement anyway; every research effort needs one
Skip the research until a decision emerges from the roadmap
Label the work as exploration, and do not later present it as settling a decision
Choose the cheapest method available and see what turns up
questions.explanation: This is the boundary of the model. Exploration is legitimate. Manufacturing a fake decision statement to authorize it (A) is worse than labelling it honestly. The failure mode is presenting exploratory output as if it settled a decision it was never designed to settle.

questions.question: A research readout concludes: "Users want a faster onboarding experience." Why is this weak as a finding?
options: It is not quantified with a percentage
Onboarding is an engineering concern, not a product one
It should have come from behavioural data rather than interviews
It states a preference as a conclusion without naming the decision it changes or what it rules out
questions.explanation: A finding phrased as a universal preference cannot displace any alternative, so no decision moves. The most tempting distractor is C — blaming the method. But behavioural data phrased the same way would fail for exactly the same reason, so the method is not the failure here.
